How To Build an Employee Onboarding Process That Sticks

A strong employee onboarding process can help new hires feel confident, connected, and ready to contribute. In this video, learn the difference between employee onboarding and orientation, and explore the four stages of onboarding: preparing for the first day, creating a welcoming experience, setting expectations during the first week, and checking progress during the first month. You will also learn about important new hire paperwork, including Form I-9, Form W-4, state tax withholding forms, and required notices. See how Paychex Flex® Onboarding can help organize onboarding forms, tasks, and follow-ups in one place, or use the complete new hire onboarding checklist for a deeper step-by-step guide.

For additional context, employers can learn more about the importance of onboarding new hires, review background checks, create an employee handbook, and support ongoing employee training through related Paychex resources.

Introduction

0:01 You hired the right person, but now here's the part that decides whether they stay, the first few weeks. So, let me show you how to do onboarding right.

0:16 First, a quick distinction people often mix up.

The difference between employee onboarding and orientation

0:21 Orientation is a day. Onboarding is a journey. A strong onboarding process runs from before someone starts all the way through their first few months. And it's what turns a nervous first day into long-term success. So, here's the big picture. Great onboarding moves through four stages. Get the sequence right and new hires feel confident, connected, and ready to contribute.

Stage 1: Before the first day

0:57 Stage one, before they even show up, send a welcome email with the start date, dress code, and schedule. Set up their accounts. Knock out paperwork early. Just be mindful that depending on worker classification, and location, you may need to compensate for time spent before day one. So, check your wage and hour rules.

1:23 Handle the backstage stuff ahead of time. The forms, the computer, the gear. Do it now and day one shifts from administrative headaches to real connection.

Stage 2: The first day

1:39 Next, the first day. This is where new hires get overwhelmed. Names, systems, and expectations all at once. So, keep it human. Give a tour. Introduce the team. Assign a mentor or onboarding buddy. Walk through the role and share what your company stands for.

Stage 3: The first week

2:01 Stage three, the first week. This sets the tone. Set up orientation on culture, policies, and benefits. Meet with managers to clarify expectations. Start training on your systems and workflows. and then walk through how your team actually communicates.

Stage 4: The first month

2:24 And finally, stage four, the first month. By now, they should have a real grip on the role. Review performance goals, run a progress check-in, and encourage them to start contributing to real projects. Then keep asking what's going well, what's unclear, and what's next.

The compliance paperwork

2:45 An important reminder, one thing you can't skip, the compliance paperwork. Form I9, form W4, any state tax withholding forms, required new hire notices, and your employee handbook with confirmed receipt. Handle all this early and you protect both your business and your new hire's first impression. And this is exactly where paychecks comes in. Everything we just walked through, the forms, the tasks, the follow-ups, Paychecks Flex onboarding keeps it all in one place so nothing slips through the cracks. You add your new hire, assign the onboarding tasks. You can use our pre-made ones or fully customize your own, and your new hire takes it from there, completing everything from wherever they are.

How Paychex helps

3:41 You stay organized and audit ready and they get a first day that feels welcoming instead of chaotic. That's the difference between a checklist you're chasing and a process that runs itself. Now you can put your time where it matters most, helping your people grow.

4:01 And that's the framework. For the full step-by-step checklist, the link is below. And if this helped, be sure to hit subscribe for more HR guidance.
